More importantly, the agreement contains no fair value assessment or justification at all — there is no analysis of the relationship between the price charged (interest, fees, administration/arrangement charges) and the benefits provided to the consumer. Excerpt [2] establishes that manufacturer firms "must consider all the costs and charges a consumer may incur" when assessing the price charged, and excerpt [4] confirms this extends to "all interest, fees and charges a consumer may incur" for consumer credit products like personal loans. Excerpt [5] further requires that "firms must still be able to demonstrate that the benefits were reasonable relative to the price" and that firms must consider how charging structures are designed. The document's explicit statement that fair value justification is "Not addressed in this document" is a direct gap against this requirement — the retrieved excerpts show that firms must actively assess and be able to demonstrate fair value, not merely disclose that fees exist and may vary. The ability to vary the tariff "from time to time" with only "reasonable notice" (clause 6.3), absent any fair value framework governing how such charges are set or reviewed, compounds the concern, as there is no indication the administration/arrangement charges or their variation have been assessed for fair value as required.

9. VULNERABLE CUSTOMERS
9.1 The Lender recognises that some customers may, either permanently or
    temporarily, be in circumstances that make them vulnerable — for example
    due to ill health, bereavement, changes in personal circumstances, low
    resilience to financial or emotional shocks, or low capability in
    managing financial matters.
9.2 If the Borrower considers that they are, or may become, in such
    circumstances, they are encouraged to let the Lender know, in
    confidence, by contacting the customer service team using the details in
    clause 8. The Lender will work with the Borrower to identify appropriate
    support, which may include adjusted communication methods, additional
    time to consider options, or referral to independent debt advice.
9.3 Contacting the Lender under this clause will not affect the Borrower's
    obligations under this Agreement, but may affect the options available
    to the Borrower if they experience payment difficulties.

10. DATA PROTECTION
10.1 The Lender will process the Borrower's personal data in accordance with
     its privacy notice, a copy of which has been provided separately.
